title: Finite-strain plane-stress and thin-three-dimensional patch cross-check
purpose: Independently check the local P33=0 membrane condensation against the same material and homogeneous deformation evaluated by a genuine three-dimensional finite-element cuboid.
physics: compressible Neo-Hookean finite strain under homogeneous uniaxial stretch with traction-free lateral and thickness directions

execution.evidence: A Q1 hexahedral thin cuboid is assigned the three-dimensional affine deformation recovered from the two-dimensional plane-stress local solve. Volume-averaged UFL first-Piola stress and energy are compared at two reference thicknesses and two cell layouts.

observables: Condensed in-plane first-Piola stress and thickness stretch.
Thin-three-dimensional volume-averaged first-Piola tensor and strain-energy density.
Deformation Jacobian and traction-free transverse stress ratio.
Relative in-plane stress and energy differences.
acceptance: The maximum in-plane nominal-stress difference is below 1e-10 relative.
The strain-energy-density difference is below 1e-10 relative.
All nominal stress components other than the loaded axial component remain below 1e-10 relative.
Changing reference thickness and through-thickness cell count does not change the homogeneous response.
limitations: This is an affine patch and geometry-assumption cross-check, not a thin-three-dimensional crack simulation.
It does not establish general near-incompressible locking control on distorted or bending-dominated meshes.
It does not validate plane-stress reduction for arbitrary through-thickness gradients, inertia, cohesive fronts, or out-of-plane instability.
